## Claim + dispatch

- **Session**: `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4` (`os-sam`, `domain:services` execution seat)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-11757-retire-sys-scim-provider`
- **Worktree**: `../objectstack-11757` (per-repo; ⛔ never the shared checkout; ⛔ never `git stash`)
- **Container & model**: `claude-opus-5` — the **measured quota exemption** from earlier this shift stands (a dev terminated at ~11:50Z on `You've reached your Fable 5 limit`; fable unavailable ⇒ opus, never lower).
- `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, **`needs:contract-review` added** — see below.

## Clause-② — this seat's call: **YES**, and I am adding the label rather than leaving it to be discovered

Retiring a platform object **removes a queryable/authorable surface**. That is the clause-② content limb, and the gate's own text — re-read **live** this round at `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — is unambiguous that paths do not reach it and cannot clear it:

> Clause ② is **NOT reachable from paths**: a card that changes contract accept/reject behaviour or **widens the public surface** is fable-mandatory too, judged from the card **CONTENT**. This line is a **FLOOR, never a clearance**.

⚠️ A removal is the mirror of a widening and I am treating it as in-scope rather than arguing the wording narrowly — the direction that would be embarrassing here is under-applying the control on an object deletion. `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read live in the same pass: **`claude-fable-5`**; this seat is below it. So on this card I will **not** clear the label, **not** flip the PR ready, and **not** arm auto-merge.

⚠️ **ADR-0087 registration** may also apply if the removal grades as declared-breaking. That is the gate's verdict to give, not mine to assume in either direction — the dev reports its own line.

## The two halves of the ruling that must not blur into each other

Restating because they look similar and are opposite:

- ⛔ **No data migration.** 「不需要考虑历史数据」 — no backfill, no reaper, no migrate-your-providers command, and no opportunistic cleanup of an existing row you happen to touch.
- ⭐ **The consumer sweep is step 1 of the work**, not a struck prerequisite. What the ruling struck was the census as a **blocker on the decision**; "what in this repo reads this object" is still measured, repaired, and pinned.

## Instrument discipline this card specifically needs

A retirement's whole risk is a reader you did not find, so the zero is the load-bearing claim:

- ⚠️ **A zero-hit needs a positive control FIRST** — prove the instrument finds a known reader of some *other* platform object before concluding this one has none. ⭐ And a control run through the same broken channel validates nothing.
- ⭐ **`git grep <ref>`**, not plain `grep` — the shared working tree is at an unknown state; other agents switch its HEAD.
- ⭐ **Pin identities, not counts.** "0 readers remain" without naming what was found and what was done to each is not a sweep.
- ⚠️ `grep -F` matches inside comments — **read the matched line before concluding** (this cost a false conclusion twice this shift).

## Fences

⛔ Zero `packages/spec` ownership — a spec edit means **stop and report**, it is the spec seat's. ⛔ Never `content/docs/releases/`, `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`. ⛔ **Draft PR only**; this seat does the landing, and only after a contract review at tier.

⚠️ Adjacent, not yours: **#11697** (spec parity) is a different seat and does not block you. Epic leg **1b** (provision the seven stable models) will be cut **behind** this card precisely so the two do not both move the SCIM platform-object surface at once — if you find yourself needing to add models, that is 1b and you should stop and say so.
